03 · Project · LA 08 and LA 09

Blue: the machine teaches, out loud

A multilingual training platform for industrial maintenance teams. It turns an employer's own manuals into lessons, 3D machine models and HYDRO, a voice tutor that answers a technician's spoken question in their language from those documents, or hands off to a supervisor. Presented in the deck as Insyde.

Live · staging/blue release, 15 Oct 2026

21 M

people work in India's registered factories

Annual Survey of Industries 2024–25
4.2%

of people aged 15–59 have formal vocational training

Periodic Labour Force Survey 2025
82 / 102

pages and API routes across four role portals

Codebase guide, 15 Oct 2026

Manuals nobody reads

Knowledge sits in English PDFs, CAD files and senior people's heads.

No one to ask at 2 a.m.

A night-shift operator facing an alarm has no expert beside the machine.

Completion is not competence

Clicking through slides counts as training; real skill is never proven.

One platform, three people

From the product deck

Worker learns the job on the machine

  • Step-by-step lessons on the 3D twin
  • Asks HYDRO by voice in their language
  • Works on the web or the Android app

Engineer goes deep on the system

  • Hydraulics and CNC industry packs
  • Scored simulators and test benches
  • Twin tools: explode, section, hotspots

Manager builds and signs off training

  • Turns manuals and CAD into lessons
  • Reviews every AI draft before release
  • Skill matrix and completion certificates

What it does

Status as of 15 Oct 2026

HYDRO voice tutor

Live

Hold one button and ask. Saaras transcribes, sarvam-105b answers from approved documents, bulbul speaks it back, streamed. Capped at 200 questions per person per day.

Android app

Manual in, lesson out

The content pipeline
  1. UploadPDF, Word, video, CAD or an approved web page
  2. Extractdocextract and webingest turn it into traceable passages
  3. Simplifysarvam-105b rewrites in plain words, then validated
  4. ReviewA person approves; safety items need an admin
  5. ComposeImmutable lesson versions, draft to published
  6. ProveAssigned lessons, scored benches, certificates

The Python inside it

15 source files, Python 3.12, Docker
FileRole (deck)LinesWhat it does
docextract · FastAPI web service on Render Live
app.pyThe Front Desk347HTTP front for the extractors; takes a file by sha256, caches results 24 h, answers polls.
isolate.pyThe Safe Room165Runs each extraction in a child process with time and memory limits.
pdf.pyThe Reader338PyMuPDF page text blocks and embedded figures, OCR for scanned pages.
ocr.pyThe Eyes86Tesseract OCR grouped into paragraphs with a confidence each.
sarvam.pyThe Interpreter450Sarvam Vision OCR client with typed errors for auth, rate limits, timeouts.
docx.pyThe Wordsmith466Word files to headings, paragraphs and tables. Standard library only.
video.pyThe Listener363ffmpeg plus Sarvam speech-to-text into a timed transcript.
cad.pyThe Draughtsman800Part names and notes out of STEP / DXF, never geometry.
errors.pyThe Rulebook34One ExtractError with codes, so the pipeline knows retry from give up.
webingest · background worker Prototype · declared, not running
worker.pyThe Dispatcher273Claims queued fetches from Postgres, rate-limits each host, retries up to 2 times, hands results back by RPC.
policy.pyThe Gatekeeper261Canonical URLs, per-organisation allow rules and robots.txt.
netguard.pyThe Bodyguard392SSRF-safe fetching: own DNS lookup, private IPs blocked, IP pinned, size caps.
extract.pyThe Editor273Scrapling parser: HTML to clean text, hidden text dropped, prompt injection flagged.
cad-converter · described in the deck only Prototype
handler.pyThe Heavy Lifter–OpenCascade meshes STEP files too big for WebAssembly, on ECS Fargate; built for a 260 MB CNC mill export.

Built to be trusted

Security
Row-level securityEvery tenant table is locked to its organisation in Postgres.
SSRF-safe fetchnetguard.py vets and pins every IP; private networks are unreachable.
Isolated extractionA hostile PDF runs in a child process with time and memory limits.
Humans approve AINo AI draft reaches a worker until a person reviews it.
Server-verified completionCourse completion is checked on the server, never trusted from the browser.

06 · Pitch storyboard

The pitch video, scene by scene

Nine beats across 2 min 42 s, roughly 60% business and 40% technology. Narration is Sarvam bulbul:v3; the Tamil answer is real output of sarvam-105b generated for the video.

0:02Business

The story

2 a.m. at a steel plant near Chennai. A hydraulic press stops; Ravi has a 300-page English manual and nobody to ask.

0:21Business

The problem

About 21 million factory workers; 4.2% with formal vocational training. Plants measure attendance, not skill.

0:35Business

What exists today

Course sites teach desk skills in English; corporate LMSs track clicks; chatbots answer from the internet.

0:56Tech

Input and output

In: the employer's manuals and a spoken question. Out: a cited spoken answer or a hand-off, plus approved lessons and tests.

1:17Business

How we improved

Voice first, grounded in company procedures, competency over completion, one-tap refreshers for managers.

1:34Tech

One unique element

HYDRO, the voice tutor: hold one button and ask in Tamil, Hindi or another Indian language.

1:44Tech

HYDRO, in Tamil

"If there's a leak inside the pump, the pressure will drop. The relief valve only controls high pressure."

1:57Tech

How the voice works

Saaras transcribes, sarvam-105b answers from documents, bulbul streams speech back. Next.js on Cloudflare, Supabase with RLS.

2:17Business

Business thesis

The bottleneck is skilled hands. Per-technician subscription, starting with maintenance, then six trades.

Topic
File and media handling, web scraping

Reading files of every kind

Four scripts that locate their input in the Downloads folder with pathlib, so they run on any OS, then read and report on it.

PDF text Task 1

CSV rows Task 2

Audio analysis Task 3

Polite scraper Bonus

Lab assessment02
Topic
Algorithmic problem solving
Level
Four problems marked Hard

Four hard problems

Each solved in an online judge, with the approach written up in plain words.

Best Time to Buy and Sell Stock III #123

  • One pass over the prices
  • Tracks the lowest buy and best profit of the first trade
  • Uses that profit to lower the cost of the second buy

Concatenated Words #472

  • Word list turned into a set for instant lookup
  • A DP tracker marks which prefixes split into valid words
  • A word may not be built from itself alone

Palindrome Pairs #336

  • Reverse map of every word
  • Each word split at every position
  • Palindromic front or back looks up its partner

Longest Valid Parentheses #32

  • Counts opening and closing brackets
  • Records the length whenever the counts match
  • A second, reverse scan catches what the first missed
Lab assessment04
Topic
Multithreading and thread pools
Libraries
threading, concurrent.futures, time, requests, urllib3

Threads and pools

Seven timed tasks that show how much wall-clock time concurrency saves, followed by two thread programs and a poster explaining a priority queue.

2.0 sTwo threads, each sleeping 2 s (Task 1)
2.0 sTen threads, each sleeping 2 s (Task 2)
10.0 sTen threads sleeping 1 to 10 s (Tasks 3–5)
5.0 smap() over threads for 5, 4, 3, 2, 1 s (Task 6)
0.21 sThreaded MP4 download (Task 6)
1.18 sTwo MP3s, each timed and sized (Task 7)

Manual threads Tasks 1–3

Create, start and join threads by hand, then in a loop, then with an argument per thread.

Thread pools Tasks 4–5

ThreadPoolExecutor with submit, collecting results with as_completed and list comprehensions.

Real I/O Tasks 6–7

map() builds a thread per item; downloads a video, then two MP3s with per-file size and time.

Thread programs Extra

Numbers and letters printed by two interleaved threads; a threading.Thread subclass with its own run().

Task 4 · thread poolexcerpt
with concurrent.futures.ThreadPoolExecutor() as executor:
    # Use list comprehension to submit 10 tasks and store the "Future" objects
    futures = [executor.submit(do_something, i) for i in range(1, 11)]

    # As each thread finishes, grab and print its return value
    for future in concurrent.futures.as_completed(futures):
        print(future.result())

Lab assessment10
Topic
Machine learning
Dated
22 Oct 2026
Libraries
pandas, numpy, scikit-learn, matplotlib, seaborn, joblib

Loan eligibility model

A loan dataset of 614 records and 13 columns, investigated, cleaned and used to train a Random Forest that is tuned, saved and tested. Accuracy figures are as printed in the submitted notebook.

614 × 13Records and columns
422 / 192Eligible (Y) / not eligible (N), about 69% Y
75.61%Initial model accuracy
81.87%Training accuracy after tuning
78.05%Testing accuracy after tuning

Investigate Step 1

Shape, types, missing values, duplicates, statistical summary, unique counts, class balance, correlation matrix and histograms.

Prepare and train Step 2

New TotalIncome and LoanToIncome columns; "3+" dependents made numeric; median and mode imputation, scaling and one-hot encoding in a ColumnTransformer.

Improve Step 3

GridSearchCV over trees (100, 200) and depth (3, 5, 8, none) with 5-fold StratifiedKFold; the better model saved with joblib.

Prevent overfitting Step 4

  • Stratified train–test split
  • Cross-validation
  • Limited tree depth
  • Minimum sample requirements
  • Feature preprocessing
Preprocessing and model pipelineexcerpt
j=ColumnTransformer([("numeric",h,f),("categorical",i,g)])
k=Pipeline([("preprocessor",j),("classifier",RandomForestClassifier(...))])
p=GridSearchCV(estimator=k,param_grid=o,cv=StratifiedKFold(n_splits=5, ...))
p.fit(a,d)
joblib.dump(q,"loan_eligibility_model.pkl")
08 · OOP question sets · created by students

Six problems, rewritten as classes

Each LeetCode problem is reframed as a real-world class design, with a problem statement, test data, processing steps, the expected result, why object-oriented design fits, and a hint.

Easy · 2Medium · 2Hard · 2
Easy 1#2032 Two Out of Three ↗

Important alerts across three monitorsclass AlertAnalyzer

Three monitoring systems each report alert IDs. An alert is important if at least two different systems report it. Return the IDs in ascending order, counting repeats within one system only once.

Test data
System 1 = [1, 2, 3, 4] System 2 = [2, 3, 5] System 3 = [3, 4, 6] Minimum systems = 2
Expected result
Important Alerts = [2, 3, 4]

OOP: encapsulation keeps the monitoring data and the analysis together inside AlertAnalyzer.

Processing steps and hint
  1. Create an AlertAnalyzer with the three lists.
  2. Treat repeats within one system as one report.
  3. Count how many systems reported each alert.
  4. Alerts 2, 3 and 4 occur in at least two systems.
  5. Alerts 1, 5 and 6 occur in only one.
  6. Sort the selected IDs.

Hint: track which systems reported each alert rather than total occurrences.

Easy 2#2124 All A's Before All B's ↗

Validating arrivals and departuresclass EventSequenceValidator

A sequence holds only A (arrival) and B (departure) events. It is valid if every A comes before any B; the validator also reports the position of the first violation.

Test data
Event Sequence = "AAABB"
Expected result
Valid Sequence = True First Violation = -1

OOP: the validator holds the sequence and its current validation state, and exposes methods for validation and violation reporting.

Processing steps and hint
  1. Create an EventSequenceValidator.
  2. Scan left to right.
  3. Before the first B, A and B are allowed.
  4. Once B appears, the departure-started state begins.
  5. Any A after that is a violation.
  6. No such A occurs in AAABB, so it is valid.

Hint: once the first B appears, think about what is still allowed.

Medium 1#491 Non-decreasing Subsequences ↗

Distinct non-decreasing runsclass SequenceAnalyzer

Find every distinct subsequence that keeps the original order and never decreases, with an extra requirement: the caller sets a minimum length.

Test data
Numbers = [4, 6, 7, 7, 5] Minimum Length = 3
Expected result
[4, 6, 7], [4, 6, 7, 7], [4, 7, 7], [6, 7, 7]

OOP: encapsulation and abstraction let the object manage the sequence, current candidate, results and minimum length while hiding the search.

Processing steps and hint
  1. Create a SequenceAnalyzer.
  2. Store the sequence and minimum length.
  3. Build subsequences preserving order.
  4. Add a value only if it is ≥ the last one chosen.
  5. Ignore subsequences shorter than 3.
  6. Remove duplicates and return the rest.

Hint: build one element at a time, and watch for duplicate values at the same decision level.

Medium 2#2024 Maximize the Confusion of an Exam ↗

The longest run of identical answersclass ExamOptimizer

An answer sheet holds only T and F, and at most K answers may change. Return the longest run of identical answers possible, and whether T or F gives it.

Test data
Answers = "TTFTTFTT" K = 2
Expected result
Max Consecutive = 5 Best Answer = T

OOP: ExamOptimizer bundles the answers, the change limit and the optimisation as one reusable object.

Processing steps and hint
  1. Create an ExamOptimizer.
  2. Try maximising a run of T.
  3. Keep a moving range and count F inside it.
  4. If F exceeds K, shrink the range.
  5. Repeat for runs of F.
  6. Return the larger of the two.

Hint: keep a window and limit how many opposite answers it holds.

Hard 1#996 Number of Squareful Arrays ↗

Access codes with square sumsclass CodeArrangementManager

Arrange numeric access codes so every adjacent pair sums to a perfect square. Generate all distinct arrangements, handle duplicates and count them; the user may fix a starting code.

Test data
Codes = [1, 17, 8] Starting Code = 1
Expected result
Valid = [[1, 8, 17]] Total = 1

OOP: abstraction hides the search behind operations such as finding arrangements and checking transitions; encapsulation keeps the state private.

Processing steps and hint
  1. Create a CodeArrangementManager.
  2. The first code must be 1.
  3. 1 + 8 = 9, a square, so 8 can follow.
  4. 1 + 17 = 18 is not, so 17 cannot.
  5. 8 + 17 = 25, a square.
  6. [1, 8, 17] is the only valid arrangement.

Hint: check the adjacent sum before extending, and track which duplicate occurrences are used.

Hard 2#220 Contains Duplicate III ↗

Suspicious sensor readingsclass SensorMonitor

A stream of integer readings. A pair is suspicious if the readings are at most K positions apart and differ by at most T. Use a sliding window instead of comparing every pair.

Test data
Readings = [1, 5, 9, 1] K = 3, T = 0
Expected result
Suspicious Pair = True

OOP: SensorMonitor holds the readings, K, T and the monitoring state, and hides the data structure behind the active window.

Processing steps and hint
  1. Create a SensorMonitor.
  2. Process readings left to right.
  3. Keep only readings within K positions.
  4. 5 differs from 1 by 4: no match.
  5. 9 has no value within 0.
  6. The earlier 1 is exactly K away with difference 0, so a pair exists.

Hint: use a structure that quickly finds a value close to the current one, and drop readings that leave the window.

Best practices

  • Keep business logic apart from the interface
  • Prefer ttk for modern widgets; grid for forms
  • Schedule updates with after(), never sleep()
  • Validate input on FocusOut or KeyRelease
